street_smart.title: A relative shares a link in your family WhatsApp group to a viral 'AI Time Machine' app that turns any selfie into a 1980s-style photo — exactly the trend Bengaluru police issued a public warning about today. Everyone in the group has already uploaded a photo and is comparing results. You open the link: it wants full gallery access and your phone number for an OTP before it will generate your free avatar, then prompts you to enter card details for a small 'watermark removal' fee afterward. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru story: city police publicly warned social media users against the viral '1980s avatar' AI photo trend, per TOI. This scenario widens that into the actual data-harvesting and payment-trap mechanism behind viral photo-filter apps. This topic (AI photo-filter/viral-trend privacy scam) has not been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The app has thousands of downloads and your relatives are vouching for it in the group, but you don't recognise the developer's name.

choices.text: Skip any app that asks for full gallery access, phone/OTP verification, or card details just to apply a filter — either look for a version that works locally in-browser without an account, or sit the trend out entirely, and never enter payment details for a supposedly 'free' filter.
choices.feedback: Correct. The real risk in trends like this isn't the filtered photo — it's the bundle of permissions and payment prompts riding along with it. A genuinely free filter has no reason to need your OTP, full gallery, or card number, and that's exactly the pattern Bengaluru police flagged today.

choices.text: Go ahead and enter your card details for the one-time watermark-removal fee since it's only a small amount and you've already shared your photo anyway.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A tiny 'test' charge is a classic way to validate a card before larger unauthorised charges follow, or to resell the card data outright. There's no legitimate reason to pay anything to remove a watermark from a 'free' viral filter.

choices.text: Share your phone number and complete the OTP step, but stop short of entering card details, so you can still join in with your family.
choices.feedback: Risky. Even without payment, handing over your phone number and OTP lets an unverified app link your identity to your photo and use both for purposes you never agreed to — from spam and SIM-swap attempts to reselling your data — and many such apps are run by developers who can't be traced.

choices.text: Upload the photo but decline every other permission or payment prompt that follows.
choices.feedback: Risky. Uploading your face to an unverified server carries its own risk even without payment or phone details — that image can be stored, reused, or fed into other tools, including for building deepfakes, once it leaves your device.

takeaways: Never hand over OTP/phone verification, full gallery access, or payment details for a 'free' photo filter — that data is the actual thing being collected, not the filter.
Before installing any viral trend app, check its publisher name, review history, and permissions list on the Play Store rather than trusting a link forwarded in a group.
If you've already used such an app, watch your bank statement for small unrecognised charges over the next few weeks and revoke its account access wherever you can.

quiz.why: The crackdown covered around 17,000 workplaces across the state; suspected child labour can be reported to Childline at 1098.

quiz.why: On the summit's sidelines, Iran's President and the UAE's Crown Prince also met and backed a joint statement urging restraint in the West Asia war, per Hindustan Times.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution bars employing children below 14 in factories, mines, or hazardous jobs?
quiz.why: Article 24 sits alongside Article 21-A, which separately guarantees free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.

quiz.question: Roughly how high above sea level does Bengaluru sit, giving it a cooler climate than most tropical Indian cities?
quiz.why: Bengaluru's position on the Deccan Plateau, at roughly 900-920 metres elevation, is the main reason its evenings stay mild even in summer.
